Try the blind test

A preset of ten small numbers, applied to the weights of an image model, was meant to give character portraits a more American-comic look leaning toward animation: flat colours and clean lines, with proportions exaggerated only slightly. Its author tuned it on four characters and then froze it; the pairs below include three characters it never saw.

Here you get 14 pairs. In each, one portrait carries the preset and the other does not; which side is random. Answer by first impression. You can use the arrow keys.

Which of the two portraits looks more like an American comic leaning toward animation — flatter colours and cleaner lines?

One question first: have you already seen the base and preset pictures of this test, on page 28 or in the story?

Nothing you click is sent anywhere. At the end you can choose to share your answers.

Which of the two portraits looks more like an American comic leaning toward animation — flatter colours and cleaner lines?

Your result

The registered blind observer chose the preset in 56 of 56 pairs. Below, every pair you saw: the preset is outlined in blue.

Share your answers (optional)

This opens a GitHub issue with your answers already written in; you can read it before submitting, and nothing is sent unless you do. It needs a GitHub account. Shared answers are kept apart from the pre-registered result: most people taking this have read the description first, and some have seen the pictures.
